record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: Can quasi-one-dimensional manganite compounds be synthesized experimentally so that the large magnetoresistance effects predicted in one-dimensional models can be tested directly?

evidence.quote: Can quasi one-dimensional manganites be prepared experimentally?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the family of manganite compounds (mixed-valence oxides of the form R_{1-x}A_x MnO_3, with R a rare-earth and A a divalent alkaline-earth cation) whose electronic, magnetic, and transport properties arise from the interplay of double-exchange, superexchange, Jahn-Teller phonons, and Coulomb interactions on the Mn sublattice. Theoretical analyses of strictly one-dimensional models of such manganites (chains of Mn ions with itinerant e_g electrons coupled to localized t_{2g} spins, lattice distortions, and on-site/inter-site Coulomb terms) predict large magnetoresistance phenomena, including colossal magnetoresistance-like responses driven by competing phases and phase-separated clustered states.

The question is the following experimental-realization problem: Do there exist physically realizable manganite materials whose crystal structure confines the relevant Mn-O-Mn exchange pathways to a single spatial direction — i.e., quasi-one-dimensional manganites in which the Mn ions form effectively decoupled chains — such that these compounds can be synthesized and characterized, and the large magnetoresistance effects predicted by one-dimensional manganite models can thereby be tested directly in experiment?
artifact.status_search_result: Since the question was posed, considerable experimental progress has been made on synthesizing quasi-one-dimensional manganite nanostructures (nanowires, nanorods, nanotubes, nanobelts) and on observing enhanced magnetoresistance when manganite systems are confined toward one dimension. These efforts represent partial experimental realizations and have probed predictions of one-dimensional manganite models, although truly intrinsically quasi-1D bulk manganite compounds (analogous to quasi-1D cuprates) remain less established. The question is therefore partially solved rather than fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: One-Dimensional Perovskite Manganite Oxide Nanostructures: Recent Developments in Synthesis, Characterization, Transport Properties, and Applications
status_evidence.snippet: In the past two decades, much effort has been made to synthesize and characterize one-dimensional perovskite manganite nanostructures in the forms of nanorods, nanowires, nanotubes, and nanobelts.
status_evidence.claim: Quasi-1D manganite nanostructures have been successfully synthesized and characterized.

status_evidence.title: Spatial confinement tuning of quenched disorder effects and enhanced magnetoresistance in manganite nanowires
status_evidence.snippet: Through the confinement of a manganite system down to quasi-one-dimensional nanowires ... with reduced nanowire width, the magnetoresistance shows substantial enhancement at low temperatures.
status_evidence.claim: Quasi-1D confinement of manganites produces enhanced magnetoresistance, allowing direct experimental tests of 1D-model predictions.
